question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 10-trading-day windows of front-month WTI price return minus S&P 500 futures return; unconditionally the median is near -0.4pp (equity drift minus ~zero front-month oil drift) with ~7pp SD, but the OVX>50 subset roughly doubles that dispersion, which is the regime we are in. Center stays just below zero: futures are near-martingale, so the only tilts are equity drift and the right-skew of a supply-disruption oil distribution (median < mean). Dispersion does the work - oil at 3-4% daily swings, an unrepaired Saudi East-West pipeline with a contested repair ETA (days per DOE, weeks per satellite analysts), Hormuz traffic down 95%, and an inverse oil-equity correlation that makes both legs push the difference the same way. Sell-side is split 85 to 140+ on Brent, so neither tail is speculative. A further ambiguity I could not resolve - CLV26 expires ~Sep 22, day two of the window, and a naive front-month series rolls down by the steep backwardation while a roll-adjusted index earns positive roll yield - adds a couple of points of width, not direction. Escapes priced off concrete mechanisms: a Hormuz-reopening/repair unwind (Goldman 85 base case) below -25, permanent infrastructure damage (BofA 150 case) above +25. Thin spot: no market prices this spread, and the question text ships no resolution criteria, so the measurement convention is genuinely unknown - which argues for staying near the reference class rather than sharpening.

calls.reconciliation: No web access this run; reconciled on the dossiers. Settled factually: (a) the Sep 16 FOMC hike is DONE, 25bp to 3.75-4.00% unanimous under Warsh with the S&P closing roughly flat - Run 3 retrieved after the 14:00 ET decision while Runs 1-2 retrieved before, and it is pre-window in all three readings; (b) the next OPEC+ meeting is Oct 4, after the window, corroborated independently by Runs 2 and 3, with October quotas already fixed flat on Sep 6 - Run 1's 'not found' is resolved; (c) the Sep employment report falls Fri Oct 2 08:30 ET, inside the window before the 16:00 ET resolution; (d) no matching human market exists - Kalshi's WTI contracts are single-leg absolute-level ladders with running-max resolution and no S&P leg, so they are not an anchor, and the lines.com pipeline-restart market was unreadable (403). I also trim Run 2's -15.5 p10 to -13.5: the premium-unwind skew is real, but 2-3 sessions elapse before measurement opens, so a DOE-style fast restart partly resolves outside the window, and 4% is already priced below -25.
